negative: Expect a simulation callback without registering it through vpi_register_cb().
positive: Register a simulation callback through vpi_register_cb() and trigger its reason.

edge: Register two callbacks with different reasons and distinguish their invocations.
positive: Register a distinctive callback reason and verify invocation only for that reason.

edge: Register two routines for separately registered callbacks.
positive: Register a distinctive callback routine and verify that routine is invoked at the selected reason.

edge: Use a callback reason for which no associated object is required.
positive: Register a value-change callback for one selected net and verify the callback identifies that net.

edge: Use one callback routine with different user_data in two registrations.
positive: Register distinctive user_data and verify the callback receives the same value.

edge: Use a net value change as a minimal event and verify one corresponding callback.
notes: Select an exact callback reason defined by the VPI API for materialization.
positive: Register an applicable simulation-event callback and trigger its specified event.

edge: Request a callback after a small nonzero delay.
notes: Select an exact callback reason defined by the VPI API for materialization.
positive: Register an applicable simulation-time callback and verify invocation at its requested simulation-time condition.

edge: Use normal end of simulation rather than a tool-specific interactive feature.
notes: Select a portable callback reason defined by the VPI API.
positive: Register an end-of-simulation callback and verify invocation when simulation completes.

edge: Use the startup callback to register one user-defined system task, without depending on vendor-specific loading options.
positive: Register through the normative startup mechanism and record invocation during tool startup before design processing.

edge: Use a source occurrence that executes zero times and verify no calltf call.
negative: Invoke calltf only once for multiple runtime executions.
positive: Execute an associated system task repeatedly in a loop and count one calltf invocation per iteration.

edge: Use both mechanisms with the same selected mode while observing one compatible legacy behavior.
positive: Use a host-default mode for one unbound application and a different compile-bound mode for another application in the same run.

edge: Compare preprocessing of the same source with and without a compatibility symbol.
negative: Ignore the selected mode and bind a designated API directly to current behavior.
positive: Preprocess calls to several designated APIs under a compatibility symbol and verify each resolves to its mode-specific form.

negative: Define two listed symbols before vpi_user.h and require a C compilation error.
positive: Compile with exactly one listed compatibility symbol.

edge: Put a callback in a separate unit.
negative: Use different compatibility symbols across VPI-accessing units.
positive: Build a multi-source application with the same selection in every VPI-accessing unit.

edge: Select a listed mode through the compiler command line rather than source.
negative: Define a compatibility symbol after including vpi_user.h.
positive: Define `VPI_COMPATIBILITY_VERSION_1800v2023` to 1 before including VPI headers.

edge: Place the occurrence in source that is compiled but never executed.
positive: Register compiletf and record its invocation while a source occurrence is parsed, before simulation starts.

edge: Put an invocation in source that is not executed at runtime and still observe one compiletf call for that source instance.
negative: Call compiletf repeatedly for one source instance.
positive: Place two source invocations of a registered name and count one compiletf call for each.

negative: Attempt to obtain different per-application modes solely through multiple host defaults in one run.
positive: Run one unbound application under the host default and another application compiled with a different compatibility symbol.

edge: Register a callback for completion of tool execution.
negative: Expect an unregistered application routine to be invoked for a simulation activity.
positive: Register a value-change callback and observe invocation when the selected net changes.

edge: Repeat an applicable operation later in simulation to confirm availability continues.
positive: In a cbEndOfCompile callback, perform a portable VPI object-access operation unavailable during startup.

edge: Contrast an unbound application with one having an explicit compile-bound selection.
positive: Select a host default compatibility mode and load an application compiled without a compatibility symbol; verify the selected legacy behavior.

edge: Use two instances whose corresponding objects initially have equal values but distinct identities.
negative: Alias corresponding objects from two instances to one VPI handle/object identity.
positive: Instantiate one module twice and obtain distinct VPI objects and values for the same declared wire in each instance.

negative: Expect vpiRefObj results.
positive: Iterate vpiInterfaceDecl on an allowed source and verify vpiVirtualInterfaceVar results.

edge: Contrast vpiClassDefn.
positive: Obtain a vpiClassTypespec for an active scope and iterate vpiInterfaceDecl/vpiVirtualInterfaceVar.

edge: Use a nested operation and inspect each operation node separately.
positive: Inspect a binary source expression and verify its expression handle has vpiOperation type.

negative: Attempt an object-access VPI operation from sizetf that becomes available only after cbEndOfCompile begins.
positive: Within sizetf, limit VPI calls to functionality available in the preceding startup stage.

negative: Request vpiInterfaceDecl iteration on vpiClassDefn.
positive: Inspect vpiClassDefn without the removed relation.

negative: Attempt to assign two different host-default modes within the same simulation run.
positive: Run multiple unbound VPI applications under one selected host-default compatibility mode.

edge: Use parentheses to make the outer and inner operation relationship unambiguous.
positive: Traverse a nested expression and verify the outer operation contains operand handles for subexpressions evaluated before it.

edge: Invoke the override with minimum-width and much wider arguments in the same design.
negative: Provide an override whose return width varies per invocation according to argument width.
positive: Override $signed with a sizetf routine and invoke it with differently sized arguments, observing one fixed return width.

edge: Override $signed or $unsigned and test fixed-width behavior separately.
positive: Associate a PLI application with a built-in system function name and observe that invocation executes the replacement.

edge: Use occurrences in multiple scopes while retaining one registration.
positive: Place multiple occurrences of one associated user-defined system function in the design and count one sizetf invocation.

edge: Compare a design containing the function with one containing no occurrence.
positive: Register sizetf for a user-defined system function that appears once in the design and record that sizetf is called.

edge: Return a width of one bit from sizetf.
negative: Have calltf provide a result width inconsistent with sizetf.
positive: Return a distinctive width from sizetf and provide that many result bits from calltf.

edge: Compare otherwise similar vpiRealFunc and vector-function registrations.
positive: Register a vpiRealFunc with a sizetf pointer and verify an occurrence does not invoke sizetf.

edge: Provide both compiletf and calltf for the same task and count sizetf separately.
positive: Register a user-defined system task with a sizetf pointer and verify executing or compiling task occurrences does not invoke it.

edge: Register `cbStartOfSimulation` at startup, then register broader callbacks when that callback runs.
negative: Register a value-change callback directly from a startup routine.
positive: Register each permitted startup callback reason from separate startup configurations.

edge: Perform other VPI access later from the registered start-of-simulation callback.
negative: Call an object-access VPI routine directly from a startup routine.
positive: From a startup routine, register a system task and an allowed callback.

negative: Use SystemVerilog-specific VPI declarations without including sv_vpi_user.h.
notes: Use the normative header declarations rather than locally redeclaring the API.
positive: Compile a C PLI application using SystemVerilog-specific VPI declarations with sv_vpi_user.h included.

edge: Return a value with high bits set to expose whether the width is exactly 32.
positive: Register an integer/vector system function without sizetf and verify its expression width is 32 bits.

edge: Exercise each of the three callback roles separately with the same signature shape.
negative: Define a systf callback as a zero-argument or multi-argument C function.
positive: Define registered sizetf, compiletf, and calltf callbacks using the normative one-argument callback signature.

edge: Register different user_data values for separate system names sharing a callback and distinguish invocations by the received value.
positive: Register a distinctive user_data pointer and verify the invoked callback receives that exact value.

edge: Register a system task and a system function separately through the same API.
positive: Call vpi_register_systf with a complete registration record, then invoke the registered system name from SystemVerilog.

edge: Register a task referenced from an early-elaborated scope.
negative: Delay system-task registration until after reference resolution.
positive: Call vpi_register_systf from startup before elaboration, then resolve and invoke the registered task.

edge: Write a writable variable tfarg through the applicable PLI routine and observe the source-level variable update.
notes: Materialization requires a compiled PLI component; test the callback calling convention separately.
positive: In a PLI callback, read an invocation argument through the task/function-argument access routines.

edge: Invoke the same callback from calls with different tfarg counts; its C callback parameter convention remains unchanged.
negative: Define the callback as though each SystemVerilog tfarg were passed as a matching C parameter.
positive: Invoke a registered callback from a user-defined system call with tfargs and use the callback form prescribed by VPI rather than expecting corresponding C parameters.

edge: Contrast registration of an overridable built-in system task with a timing-check name.
negative: Attempt to register a PLI replacement for a timing check name such as `$setup`.

edge: Invoke a user-defined system task with no arguments and another with multiple arguments.
positive: Invoke a registered user-defined system task with a string and a variable argument.

edge: Use it in an expression constrained by its registered return type and width.
positive: Use a registered user-defined system function invocation in a value expression.

edge: Verify argument modification separately from setting the function result.
notes: Writability remains governed by applicable object and VPI access rules.
positive: Pass a writable variable to a registered user-defined system function and have its callback update that tfarg.

edge: Read multiple tfargs while independently setting the result.
positive: Pass a known value to a registered user-defined system function and have its callback read that tfarg.

edge: Verify the returned value independently of tfarg modifications.
positive: Have a registered callback set a known function result and consume it in a SystemVerilog expression.

edge: Use sizetf to define a one-bit vector result.
negative: Omit required sizing behavior for a vector-valued user system function and assume an argument-derived width.
positive: Define a vector-valued system function whose sizetf returns a distinctive width and verify expression sizing.

edge: Place the distinguishing character far beyond a conventional short identifier length.
positive: Register two otherwise identical legal user-defined system names that differ only in a late character and verify each invokes its own callback.

edge: Change the case of exactly one letter in an invocation and verify it does not select the differently cased name.
positive: Register two otherwise identical user-defined system names differing only in letter case and invoke each.

edge: Use a `$`-prefixed name with a digit immediately after the prefix.
negative: Attempt a user-defined system name containing punctuation other than dollar sign or underscore.
positive: Register a `$`-prefixed name containing letters, digits, underscores, and an additional dollar sign.

edge: Use a short legal name such as $a.
negative: Attempt to register a user-defined system task name whose first character is a letter.
positive: Register and invoke a user-defined system task whose name begins with $.

edge: Use a long legal name that differs from another registered name only near its end.
notes: Choose a practical but conspicuously long name; this rule does not prescribe implementation resource limits.
positive: Register and invoke a user-defined system task whose legal name is substantially longer than ordinary identifiers.

edge: Distinguish a writable variable argument from a non-writable expression.
notes: Writability remains governed by applicable object and VPI access rules.
positive: Pass a writable variable to a registered user-defined system task and have its callback update the tfarg.

negative: Attempt to use a user-defined system task invocation as a value-producing expression.
positive: Invoke a registered user-defined system task as a statement without consuming a result.

edge: Read arguments of different SystemVerilog value types through applicable VPI access forms.
positive: Pass a known value to a registered user-defined system task and have its callback read that tfarg.

edge: Use the task as a standalone subroutine call statement.
positive: Invoke a registered user-defined system task in a context where a void function call is permitted.

edge: Use a legal expression combining multiple operator levels.
notes: Choose expression forms with explicit VPI object mappings in Clauses 37 and 38.
positive: Obtain a VPI handle for a source expression containing nested operators.

edge: Use separate callbacks triggered during compilation and execution.
negative: Treat a standalone executable as the callback body without linking it into the tool.
notes: Materialization requires the implementation's supported PLI loading/linking procedure.
positive: Build a C callback into a loadable PLI component and invoke it from a registered user-defined system name.

edge: Avoid an intervening VPI call between the failing operation and status query.
notes: Choose an error condition whose invalidity is explicitly defined by the VPI API.
positive: Cause a specified VPI routine error, immediately call vpi_chk_error(), and verify a nonzero result.

edge: Query immediately after a VPI operation chosen to have well-defined status.
positive: Build and call a PLI application that invokes vpi_chk_error().

edge: Apply compatibility only to a compatible partition of a mixed design.
negative: Assume an old compatibility mode enables an old application to process newer constructs outside that mode's model.
positive: Run an older VPI application under a matching compatibility mode against a design using only constructs compatible with that mode.

negative: Use core VPI declarations without including vpi_user.h.
notes: Use the normative header declarations rather than locally redeclaring the API.
positive: Compile a C PLI application using a core VPI routine with vpi_user.h included.

edge: Distinguish the array object from an element.
negative: Expect the array object itself to have vpiIntegerVar type.
positive: Inspect an unpacked integer array as vpiRegArray and a non-array integer variable as vpiIntegerVar.

negative: Expect the array object's vpiType to be legacy vpiMemory.
positive: Inspect an unpacked one-dimensional reg array and verify its object type is vpiRegArray.

edge: Verify returned objects use current vpiRegArray type rather than vpiMemory object type.
positive: Use the vpiMemory one-to-many transition from an applicable scope to access current array objects.

edge: Verify returned element objects have current vpiReg type rather than vpiMemoryWord object type.
positive: Use the retained vpiMemoryWord iterator on an applicable array relation and enumerate its current element objects.

negative: Expect the element object's vpiType to be legacy vpiMemoryWord.
positive: Inspect an element of an unpacked one-dimensional reg array and verify its object type is vpiReg.

edge: Compare unary and binary operation nodes.
positive: Read vpiOpType from a vpiOperation handle for an operator with known arity and enumerate the expected operands.

edge: Distinguish the array object from an element.
negative: Expect the array object itself to have vpiRealVar type.
positive: Inspect an unpacked real array and verify its array object is vpiRegArray.
Verify both alias constants designate the same object type.
Iterate vpiReg on a vpiRegArray representing integer or time elements and verify corresponding non-vpiReg elements are returned.
Verify both alias constants designate the same object type.
Iterate vpiRegArray in a scope containing integer, time, real, and reg/logic arrays and observe each.

edge: Distinguish the array object from an element.
negative: Expect the array object itself to have vpiTimeVar type.
positive: Inspect an unpacked time array as vpiRegArray and a non-array time variable as vpiTimeVar.
Iterate vpiVariables in a scope containing a scalar reg/logic variable and a reg/logic array and observe both.
